Subject: EU-only processing + egress restrictions

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the demo last week. Our security and legal teams raised two critical questions we need answered before starting a pilot: 1) can you guarantee that customer data and model inference never leave EU compute (including backups and DR failover)? 2) We need a short list of technical controls and contractual language (SCCs + any supplemental commitments) that would allow us to satisfy our Schrems II review.

Specifically:
- Are logs, metrics and the control plane stored outside the EU? If so, can they be restricted?
- How do you handle operator access for troubleshooting (does support require remote access from non-EU regions?)
- Will you agree to in-region backups and a documented deletion-and-proof process (we will need proof-of-deletion artifacts)

Can you provide a single-slide summary or doc we can take to legal this week?

Best,
Jurgen
Head of Security, Medisys

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>

Hi Jurgen — thanks for the clear list. Short answer: yes, we can support EU-only processing for the inference path and customer data; below is a concise summary you can share with legal, plus next steps. Longer technical notes attached.

High-level commitments (pilot scope):
- Compute and persistent storage for customer workloads will be hosted in the customer-chosen EU region (we currently support eu-west-1 and eu-central-1).
- Backups and snapshot storage for that workload will be configured to remain in-region; we will not replicate snapshots outside EU without explicit signed approval.
- Control plane metadata (service orchestration, billing identifiers) is hosted in our EU control plane option for enterprise customers; operator access can be constrained to EU-located SREs on contract.
- Operator access: support troubleshooting requires just-in-time (JIT) session creation; sessions are logged, require MFA, and can be restricted to SIEM forwarding or customer jump-hosts.
- SCCs: We can execute the European Commission's SCCs and provide Annex customizations in the security addendum. We also provide a supplemental Appendix that documents technical measures and access controls.
- Deletion & evidence: We will provide: deletion confirmation (timestamp + object IDs), storage-level tombstones, and a signed attestation for the deletion event. Sample evidence file attached.

Next steps:
1) I'll loop in Aditya (infra) and Naomi (legal/compliance) to answer the deeper infra and contractual questions.
2) We'll produce a 1-page control summary and a draft SCCs Appendix for your counsel in 48 hours.

Irene Choi
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: EU-only processing + egress restrictions — infra specifics

Jurgen / Irene — joining with infra detail you can paste into your tech review. Happy to jump on a call.

Technical controls (pilot configuration):
- Region pinning: workloads are pinned to a VPC in the customer's selected EU region; all compute, ephemeral caches, and persistent volumes are provisioned there.
- Network egress locks: outbound egress from the VPC is restricted by default (deny-all). Any necessary external integrations (e.g., telemetry to your SIEM) must be explicitly configured and will be scoped to endpoints you approve.
- Backups: snapshots encrypted with a customer-managed key (CMK) stored in the same region; cross-region snapshot replication is disabled.
- Control plane: we offer a customer-controlled control plane option (hosted in your VPC) for enterprise that keeps orchestration metadata in-region. For customers choosing Redwood-hosted control plane, we can provide an EU-only variant for enterprise contracts.
- Operator access model: support sessions require an access ticket, are time-limited, MFA-protected, and delivered through a customer-configured bastion (if requested). All session recordings and keystroke logs can be exported to a customer S3 bucket.
- Monitoring & logs: application logs can be configured to forward to your in-region logging account; aggregated usage metrics can be anonymized/aggregated to avoid transferring identifiers outside the EU.
- Disaster recovery: DR runbooks are documented; we offer an in-region DR plan (hot-standby in a second EU AZ) as an add-on. Cross-region DR only with explicit written approval.

Open items for contract/legal:
- Confirm scope of "control plane metadata" that must remain in-region (list below).
- Language for operator access restrictions and proof-of-deletion timeline (we propose 30 days to generate and deliver evidence).

If that looks good I'll incorporate it into the SCCs Appendix.

- Aditya
Principal Infra Engineer
